thread:
Marta Singh: FYI we just got an OSS-SEC alert about CVE-2026-21844 in yargs-deep — prototype pollution PoC circulating, reported exploited in the wild. Affects transitive deps in multiple services (cli-utils -> yargs-deep).

Alex Carter: Ack. Thanks Marta. Can you drop the advisory link and a brief impact note?

Marta Singh: https://oss-alerts.example/cve/CVE-2026-21844 — PoC manipulates __proto__ via arg parsing. Impact: arbitrary property injection during CLI parsing; some of our helper binaries parse untrusted input in request pipelines.

Jin Park: Quick triage: severity=CRITICAL, likely remote when attacker can send crafted args to parse surface. Affects explorer-service and data-ingest-worker via transitive path. Runtime exposure depends on whether untrusted strings reach parsing step.

Sam O'Neill: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) block vulnerable versions at image build (npm-force-resolutions or patch-package), 2) add a short-term application-level sanitizer to disallow `__proto__` keys before parsing, 3) WAF rules to drop suspicious payloads.

sec-bot: Vulnerability created: CVE-2026-21844 | Package: yargs-deep | Severity: CRITICAL | Status: EXPLOITED_IN_THE_WILD

Alex Carter: Priorities: (A) emergency hotfix in CI image for affected services, (B) runtime hardening where feasible, (C) org-wide dependency scan and lockfile override, (D) customer comms plan if we confirm exploitation. Assign owners: Marta(A), Jin(B), Sam(operations).

Marta Singh: Opening PRs now. Plan: bump to patched `yargs-deep@2.4.1`, add `npm-force-resolutions` in monorepo, add test that rejects `__proto__` shaped input.

Jin Park: I'll prepare a cluster admission rule to block deployment of images with vulnerable SBOM entries and add a Kibana dashboard to watch for suspicious CLI parsing errors. Also adding a short feature flag to disable CLI parsing in production processes where possible.

Sam O'Neill: ops-oncall — please prepare rebuild and staged rollout for explorer-service once Marta's PR lands. Hold canary at 10% and run smoke tests.

ops-oncall: Kicked off rebuild for explorer-service image at 1932103605. Holding canary. ETA ~25m for canary smoke.

Marta Singh: PR link: https://github.com/redwood/explorer-service/pull/542 — includes `package.json` resolutions and unit test. WIP, pushing now. :shipit:

Alex Carter: Also coordinate with legal for disclosure language and with support for possible customer outreach. Draft internal blurb: what, who, impact, mitigation, ask.

sec-bot: Triage status changed: in-progress (assigned: Marta Singh, Jin Park).

Jin Park: Canary smoke green. No obvious errors. Rolling to 50% now. Will monitor for CLI parse exceptions. :eyes:

ops-oncall: Full rollout complete at 1932103910. No regressions flagged in health checks. Rebuilt images pushed to registry with new SBOMs.

Sam O'Neill: Good job. Next: 1) run org-wide SBOM check and create PRs for any other services referencing vulnerable yargs-deep, 2) prepare post-incident vuln report, 3) decide on public advisory.

Marta Singh: Drafting customer-facing language for SOC/CS — will share here for review. Also adding timeline to incident doc.

Alex Carter: Please include exploit indicators and recommended mitigations for customers (upgrade, rebuild images, scan SBOM). Targeting internal note in 1 hour.

sec-bot: Status updated: monitoring.

Marta Singh: Postmortem doc created: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/2026-03-yargs-deep-pp (WIP).

Alex Carter: Thanks team — file the follow-up tasks and close this thread once postmortem is published.

ops-oncall: Closing operational rollout tasks. Leaving monitoring on for 72h.

Sam O'Neill: Filing vulnerability report and follow-ups now.

sec-bot: Incident state: mitigated (monitoring).
